title: SAVE trial
official: Sevoflurane vs. propofol for general Anesthesia in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with endoVascular treatmEnt (SAVE trial)
summary: Main objective: Compare the final volume of cerebral infarction by magnetic resonance imaging at 72 hours in patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing mechanical thrombectomy under general anesthesia, who are randomly assigned to receive anesthetic maintenance with sevoflurane or propofol.

interventions.name: Sevoflurano Baxter 100% líquido para inhalación del vapor EFG
Propofol Fresenius 20 mg/ml emulsión inyectable y para perfusión EFG

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age >18 years
2. Acute ischemic stroke within 24 hours from the last time seen well (LTSW), undergoing emergency endovascular treatment (EVT), with or without prior thrombolysis.
3. Intracranial occlusion in the anterior circulation, including occlusions in segments M1 and M2 of the middle cerebral artery and/or the terminal portion of the internal carotid artery (TICA). Tandem lesions affecting extracranial segments of the internal carotid artery will also be included.
4. Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) ≥6 on baseline computed tomography (CT).
5. Pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0–3.
6. Indication for general anesthesia at the start of the procedure (<30 minutes from femoral puncture) due to one of the following reasons: • Confusion or lack of patient cooperation. • Technical difficulties, such as complex arterial access, vascular tortuosity, need for extra- or intracranial stent placement, distal/medium vessel occlusions, among others. • Treating team's preference.
7. Ability of the patient or the family member/legal representative to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of hemorrhagic lesions on baseline CT.
2. Occlusions in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA).
3. Occlusions in the posterior circulation, including vertebral, basilar, or posterior cerebral arteries (PCA).
4. Hemodynamic instability.
5. Acute respiratory failure requiring orotracheal intubation
6. Decision to perform general anesthesia due to complications during the endovascular treatment.
7. Known hypersensitivity to propofol, sevoflurane, or any of their excipients.
8. Personal or family history of malignant hyperthermia, or suspected susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia (contraindication to halogenated anesthetics such as sevoflurane).
9. History of a previous severe adverse reaction to halogenated anesthetics, including hepatotoxicity associated with their use.
